steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I'm so sorry I'm late...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: This is the selections! If you were tardier by twenty minutes, we'd be hand in hand as we waltzed home!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I'm sorry...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Would you mind quickly explaining yourself?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: My... grandpa went missing this morning, actually.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Missing?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Nothing terribly serious. I found him in the Afterglow in an alley, and he said he was just up too early, out for a walk.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: For a walk, the whole time until you arrived here?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: No, no, I went to Rhodes Island this morning too, for the admission procedures.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: With your grandfather? At the Rhodes Island office?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I recall Rhodes Island having only a miniscule branch in Vyseheim. They couldn't be admitting patients.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: They couldn't, but Hibiscus gave up her own bed, and she promised she'd put my grandpa's health first.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hmph... A charming tale, but that cost you a pretty penny, didn't it?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: They took the money this morning. It was less than half of what you gave me yesterday.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Well, well. You'll have to check regularly on your grandpa, then, so they don't trim corners where you're not looking.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: 'Trim corners?'

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: They're a business, after all. Their profits have to come from the sick, if they admit them on such low fees. Say, a little from their meals, a little from their equipment and medication—

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I don't think that's what's happening.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And how do you know?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Yesterday afternoon, they gave him medicine to take before I'd paid anything.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: And Hibiscus spared some food for me this morning. I only turned her down because I was so short on time.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Such a meticulous performance. Surely your grandpa was unwilling to go precisely because he could see that.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I get it. I'll be checking in on him as much as I can.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Thank me?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I know you're taking pains to tell me all this because you're worried me or my grandfather will be hurt.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Never mind. Let's move on.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What did you think of the score after picking it up last night?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: Next entry, Ebenholz and Kreide!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Come.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Czerny is overseeing the selections today in person. We can't afford to embarrass ourselves.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Greetings, Herr Czerny.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: No need for pleasantries. Go on, begin.
The selections are quite unlike the applications, where crowds thronged the seats to watch. Save for a scant few staff, only Czerny and the entrants are present.
If yesterday's audience was present, the majority would be applauding this brief ensemble piece until their hands were raw.
But here and now, as the final lingering notes fall away, the look on Czerny's face is fearsome.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Herr Czerny?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You haven't practiced much, have you?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: As you surmised, but—

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: It smacks too strongly of being scrabbled together, you on your flute and him on his cello. There's almost no sense of coordination.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Especially from you. You were stuck fast to your own tempo, completely ignoring what the cello emoted during his melodic passage. Conversely, you forced him to accommodate for you instead.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: If you hadn't realized in time, you would have ruined the entire passage.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I would have ruined the entire passage?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: No, I feel you may not have heard quite clearly...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I'm sat right here, and you tell me I don't hear clearly? You think something's wrong with my hearing?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Herr Czerny, Ebenholz doesn't mean to offend you, he just...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Just what? All I see is someone too coddled by flattery.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Coddled by flattery?! You know nothing of my circumstances, I ask you to rescind—

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: (Hisses) Ebenholz!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I will consider Kreide. You may leave. Next.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What did you say? Do you imply even he—

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: —Herr Czerny.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: If Ebenholz isn't allowed to perform, then I can't be in this concert either.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: What's forcing you to speak for him?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Ebenholz has been a huge help to me, so...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I'm sorry, but this concert won't sink for losing one potential cellist, and losing one pot-stirrer of a Lord will pain me even less.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Next!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Scoundrel! Who does he think he is? So flippant just because he's played a piano, written a piece or two?!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Calm down, come on.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: How am I meant to be calm? What kind of attitude was that? 'Coddled by flattery?' I'm a fine, upstanding man. Who's ever coddled me? Give me a name!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I think there was just a small misunderstanding between you. Surely Herr Czerny didn't think we were that lousy...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Of course you weren't lousy, that was me! Did you forget what he said? 'I will consider Kreide. You may leave!'

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I think the sooner you apologize to him, the better. He might just let us try again.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: There's always some way, and it doesn't have to include humbling myself so badly before him!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: But... I can't think of anything that'd help other than an apology...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (Takes a deep breath)

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You return home, in any case. I'll be returning to my residence to contemplate what to do.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: If there really is no alternative, then we'll seek out Czerny.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Well... alright, then.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: 'Coddled by flattery'...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: This musician knows nothing, and he dares prattle...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Tch!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (There's the headache again...)

steps.name: Voice from Nowhere
steps.text: Useless fake...

steps.name: Voice from Nowhere
steps.text: Even the lowly blight-wracked commoners loathe the vulgar sound of your flute...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You shut up right now!

steps.name: Fretful Noble
steps.text: Mein Herr, we may not be acquainted, but you seem to be in need of some help?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Not at all... I appreciate the trouble.

steps.name: Fretful Noble
steps.text: Erm...

steps.name: Fretful Noble
steps.text: (He really is hers—)

steps.name: Fretful Noble
steps.text: Pardon my insolence.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Oh, so it's you. Do you feel unwell?

steps.name: Fretful Noble
steps.text: Er? You—what did you say? No, not at all.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Really? Your face looks somewhat sickly to me.

steps.name: Fretful Noble
steps.text: Of course not, haha, hahahaha...

steps.name: Fretful Noble
steps.text: Pardon me, pardon me...

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Your headaches are flaring up again?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It's fine. It's more or less faded by now.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I'm sorry.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What are you apologizing to me for?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I was so inconsiderate as to cause you embarrassment at the selections today, and give you a headache at that.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You were so inconsiderate?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: How did you know——

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: No, in fact it's only natural for you to know it.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Indeed. For better or worse, I am one of the sponsors of this concert, and news about it reaches me fast, Herr Ebenholz.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: You needn't worry. This is nothing major.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: In fact, I hear Czerny didn't assess you two badly at all. He intentionally designated you as backups for 'Morgen und Abend.'

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: We are more or less friends. I have him worked out to an extent.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: He's a famed artist, after all, come rain or shine, and Infected too. His temper flared up. Please, excuse him.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I do have my influence over this concert. You and Kreide can practice; I'll do Czerny's work.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'd rather redo the selections than have you exercise your sway, to be honest. This morning was merely an aberration in performance.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Of course, of course.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Still, you needn't let this perturb you so badly.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Tea? We have a citrus-flavored black tea today. They say it does good things for headaches.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Thank you very much.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: How is it?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Fragrant. I appreciate the hospitality.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Well, then, moving on. Listen closely, please.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: As you'd anticipated, my inviting you to Vyseheim, for a concert in the Infected settlement, does come with ulterior motives.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: You don't seem too bowled over.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'm used to being exploited by now.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It would've surprised me more if you had no other motive.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: In that case, I'll be straightforward.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I have a plan that's been a long time ready.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: If you act according to this plan, I have great certainty I can free you from the 'Voice of the Mundane.'

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: —What did you say?!

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: The Voice of the Mundane, Herr Ebenholz. The root of your many misfortunes, one of the legal grounds on which you possess Grafschaft of Urtica, the—

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I don't need you to explain what the Voice of the Mundane is. The thing has been inside my head all this time, tormenting me when it sees fit.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What I need you to expound on is the details of this plan.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: It's very simple. Just perform at Herr Czerny's concert as an ensemble with your fresh acquaintance Herr Kreide, and that will suffice.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Out of sheerest kindness, I'll treat this as a poor joke, Dame Gertrude.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: This is in no way a joke.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Just like you, Kreide harbors the Voice of the Mundane within him.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Him? The Voice of the Mundane?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The Twin Empresses made it explicit that I was the only one left who carried it!

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: That merely shows there are things even they don't know. To boot, it isn't even that rare.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Two Voices of the Mundane need only come close enough in space in order for 'Resonanz' to occur, and this sonority will amplify both your Arts as it occurs. That is the basis of my plan.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Beyond amplifying your Arts, Resonanz is its own kind of powerful energy, and *this* energy will be massively intensified when you two perform in ensemble.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: It just needs the appropriate induction, and I'll be able to make use of this energy to transfer your Voice of the Mundane into him.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Then what will happen to Kreide?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Fear not. I'll handle that as deemed fit.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I still don't understand, though. Why does it have to be Czerny's concert?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'll duet with Kreide at his home, you come induce this resonance, and you transfer my Voice of the Mundane into him. Won't that work?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: The induction of Resonanz is a delicate art. Alone without the Afterglow Hall, I wouldn't be able to do it.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The Afterglow Hall?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Didn't you know? Construction of the Afterglow Hall was completed under the Witch King's supervision.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I never heard.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Being a building he ordered in the twilight of his reign, the materials and architecture employed in the Hall share many resemblances to his Spire.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: It wasn't meant as the concert hall it is, synonymous with the Infected district. It was meant as a fortress of Arts, a nightmare to terrify His Majesty's enemies.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I've overstepped my bounds in doing so, but I do require the Afterglow Hall aid me in conducting the Resonanz's energy, so we can ultimately eliminate the Voice of Mundane that dwells in your body.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Do you have any other questions about the detail of this plan?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: After it's done, I will handle Kreide and any other remaining trifles. You need only hide for a suitable length of time.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Once it all blows over, you can escape your unbearable nobility once and for all, and become a free civilian.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Of course, if you aren't alright accepting such ready freedom, I won't force you, and I certainly won't make an enemy of you on the grounds that you know my plan.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Whether you wish to remain in Vyseheim until the concert concludes, or return immediately to Urtica, I will not stop you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You won't stop me...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You're the first to want to rid me of the Voice of Mundane, rather than exploit it.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Just what are you hoping to gain from me?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: A powerful assistance.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: A what?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'm just a puppet Graf. I can't even manage my own fiefs personally.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: After your supposed plan succeeds, I'll be no more than an unidentified civilian. What powerful assistance?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Fiefs, armies, even Originium Arts... none of that is important.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: What's important is the Graf Urtica gone missing, even declared dead.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Think of it. How will the Leithanian public opinion respond when at the right juncture, the Graf Urtica returns from the grave?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: To 'return from the grave.' That's the greatest aid you could ever lend me.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Please... allow me some time alone, Dame Gertrude.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I'd be glad to.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: If you wish to travel anywhere, don't hesitate to tell the servants outside.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Farewell.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Farewell. May your decision be the one that suits your interests.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Hello.
Listen. You must watch whatever happens between Kreide and Rhodes Island closely.
You may disrupt Rhodes Island's movements when necessary, but remember never to alert them at any cost. Direct military conflict is forbidden.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Allow me to report to you on Graf Urtica's circumstances...
You can save it. We know.
This is your plan. If you feel the need to expound on minor matters like this, we'll simply send someone to put you back on track.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Apologies, I was not considerate.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Ebenholz will be easy enough, but Kreide and Rhodes Island...

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I'd forgot. I have what I need, ready and waiting.
